subject: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle
messages:
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@therahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@therahealth.com>, procurement@therahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle

Laura — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm one point before we route legal: is the HIPAA onboarding / residency + KMS/HSM integration billed as a one-time implementation charge or can that be included in the monthly "compliance bundle" price?

They want the breakdown so they can decide whether to treat it as CapEx (one-off) or OpEx (recurring). If it needs to be CapEx for them, what level of discount can Redwood provide on the one-time fee versus amortizing it across a 12–24 month commitment?

Also: what are the acceptance criteria for the implementation milestone? We want to avoid back-and-forth with our internal implementation team.

—Evan

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@therahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@therahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle

Evan — appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we support both approaches; choice depends on how you want the accounting to look and how quickly you expect to scale. A quick summary below, then Ben / Rishi can add numbers: 

Options: 
- One-time implementation fee (CapEx): covers residency enablement (provisioning region-locked clusters), KMS/HSM on-boarding, audit-log export pipelines, and validation run. One-time fees are typically amortized by customers; we discount more aggressively on one-offs tied to larger term commitments.
- Fold into recurring bundle (OpEx): we increase the monthly compliance bundle charge for the pilot period (we can timebox at 12 months) and apply a smaller or no up-front fee. This lowers your initial cash outlay but results in higher TCO over a long term if the add-on stays.

Acceptance criteria we recommend including in the SOW: 
1) Residency: seeded clusters in US-East and verified cross-region access controls disabled.
2) KMS/HSM: keys provisioned, key wrap/unwrapping validated on two sample workloads.
3) Audit logs: 90-day retention in the customer's archive, ingestion into your SIEM with three sample events successfully parsed.
4) Performance: <120ms p50 for metadata operations under the pilot traffic profile.
5) Security review: passing checklist from your InfoSec (we can share our checklist).

Ben — can you attach the workback with line-item pricing and two scenarios (one-time fee with 18-month amortization and 12-month recurring bundle)? Rishi — any constraints on offering an additional 8–12% concession for lump-sum payments versus monthly billing?

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@therahealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@therahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T13:11:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle

Attaching a quick workback (price_workback.xlsx) and a draft SOW (TheraHealth_SOW_draft_v2.pdf). Highlights: 

Scenario A — One-time implementation fee (CapEx): 
- Implementation fee: $110,000 (covers residency, KMS/HSM seats for rollout, audit-log pipeline, 2 on-site workshops remotely scheduled).
- Recommended concession for lump-sum: 10% off (final: $99,000) if customer signs a 24-month commitment for dedicated capacity.
- Rationale: larger up-front covers our onboarding engineering allocation; reduces monthly charge by ~$3,800/mo when amortized over 24 months.

Scenario B — Fold into monthly bundle (OpEx): 
- No up-front implementation line; instead add $6,500/mo on top of the monthly compliance bundle for the first 12 months.
- If customer wants to cap the incremental monthly charge after 12 months, we can step it down to $1,500/mo thereafter as a maintenance premium.
- Effective 12-month cost roughly $78,000, 24-month roughly $96,000 (if stepped down after 12 months).

Other levers: 
- KMS/HSM seat pricing: we can offer an enterprise seat discount of 20% if you purchase a minimum of 3 seats.
- Audit log retention beyond 90 days: add-on priced per GB/month; large retention commitments can be discounted.

Evan, I called out the amortized monthly delta so Procurement can compare OpEx vs CapEx. Happy to walk through the workbook live.

Attachments: price_workback.xlsx (line-item by feature), TheraHealth_SOW_draft_v2.pdf

—Ben

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@therahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@therahealth.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T10:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle

Thanks — this is helpful. A few procurement clarifications: 
1) For Scenario A, would Redwood accept a milestone payment schedule? Procurement prefers 3 instalments: 40% on SOW sign, 40% on KMS/HSM provisioning, 20% on final acceptance.
2) For Scenario B, if we go with the stepped monthly approach, can the step-down be contractually guaranteed (not just a "good-faith" step-down) and tied to an objective metric (e.g., production cutover date)?
3) We need an explicit statement about audit-log ownership and exportability — SIEM ingestion must be customer-configurable without Redwood lock-in.

Also, our CFO prefers OpEx where possible, but will consider CapEx if the net present value is significantly lower over 36 months. Can you produce a 36-month TCO comparison that includes the 24-month amortization on Scenario A?

—Priya

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@therahealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA pilot: implementation fee vs. folding into monthly bundle

Priya / Team — quick answers to your bullets: 
1) Milestone schedule: yes, acceptable. We usually do 40/40/20 but can move to 35/45/20 if TheraHealth prefers more progress-based payment at provisioning.
2) Step-down guarantee: we can include a contractual step-down tied to a production cutover clause; we'll define "production cutover" in the SOW and include a Date + acceptance checklist — once met, the monthly charge steps down for the remaining term.
3) Audit-log ownership: Redwood will state in the SOW that log exports are customer-owned and we will provide configurable connectors (e.g., S3, GCS, or direct SIEM push). No vendor lock-in.

On concessions: for lump-sum payment we can extend a 10% settlement discount (as Ben proposed). For OpEx folding with a 12-month step-down, we can tighten the upfront impact to ~ $6,500/mo but offer a 6% commitment discount on the bundle if you sign a 24-month term.

Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
